object.description: In a right triangle the square on the hypotenuse equals the squares on the other two sides. The relation was known to Babylonian scribes more than a thousand years before Pythagoras, and the proof that closes Book I of Euclid's Elements, written in Alexandria around 300 BCE, is the form in which the world learned it: Euclid's textbook stayed in use for over two thousand years. It is the first equation most people ever meet, and the one that turns geometry into arithmetic.
facts: The Babylonian tablet Plimpton 322, from about 1800 BCE, lists whole-number triples such as 3, 4, 5 that satisfy the relation.
Pythagoras, who lived around 570 to 495 BCE, left no writings; the theorem was attached to his name by later Greek tradition.
Hundreds of proofs are known, including one published in 1876 by James Garfield, five years before he became president of the United States.

tour: The Pythagorean theorem as Euclid proved it in Alexandria, around 300 BCE. Beside it, a scrap of papyrus with Euclid's own diagram, a few centuries on.
